title: What If Jupiter Became a Star?

scenes.text: What if Jupiter became a star? It's closer than you think, but there's a catch.
Jupiter would need about 80 times its mass to ignite as a red dwarf star.
At about 13 times its mass, it becomes a brown dwarf, a failed star.
Even then, it would grow only roughly 10 to 20 percent wider, because gravity squeezes the extra mass in.
It would glow dim red, and the Solar System would become a binary system. Orbits could slowly destabilize.
Here's the catch. All the other planets combined hold only about 0.4 Jupiter masses. There's nothing to build it from.
